answer: Require agents to earn account creation rights by completing a randomly assigned, publicly verifiable voyage: for example, deliver a signed message through several independently operated relays, with each relay accepting only a limited number of new identities per epoch. The rule does not prove a personhood claim, but it makes mass registration consume scarce relay capacity and leaves a trace that can be audited. An attacker must recruit or control many relays, pay their operating costs, and wait across epochs; hiding keys in an ivory vault does not remove those costs.
